title: Model-tailored memory contiguity maps for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: As customers run long-context variants of Llama, Mistral, and Qwen, our serving runtime sees increased GPU memory fragmentation and suboptimal KV layout that reduces effective batch throughput. Continuous batching interacts poorly with fragmented KV allocations and quantized weights, causing headroom to be wasted and unexpected OOMs at high-concurrency regimes.

Goal: Create model-specific memory contiguity maps and allocation heuristics that reduce fragmentation and improve usable GPU headroom for long-context configs without sacrificing latency SLOs. Deliverables: (1) per-model layout profiles that specify preferred tensor ordering, preferred allocation arenas for KV vs weights vs activation buffers; (2) a runtime allocator hook that applies the profile when loading a model; (3) autoscaling signal adjustments so continuous batching respects new headroom calculations.

Scope and constraints: Focus on Llama-2 70B long-context, Mistral-XL extended context, and Qwen-7B/14B long-context variants used in hosted and dedicated modes. Profiles must be metadata-only at load time (no model weight rewrites). Changes must be safe for Dedicated and Private deployments (no cloud-provider specific APIs). Target improvements: reduce fragmentation-related memory overhead by >=18% on 2xA100-80GB pod shapes and increase median continuous-batched throughput by >=12% for 4-16 concurrent streams.

Approach:
1) Empirical profiling: run representative long-context traces (prefix, repeated prompt length distributions) to capture allocation patterns for KV cache growth, per-layer activation peaks, and peak stack usage. Produce a "contiguity heatmap" per model.
2) Derive heuristics: recommended allocation order (weights -> static KV arena -> dynamic KV arena -> activations), preferred alignment granularity for quantized kernels, and pre-reserved KV slab sizes for common long-context lengths (8k/32k/64k).
3) Runtime integration: add a model_profile JSON that the loader reads; allocator applies slab allocation for KV (first-fit within slab), uses buddy allocator fallback, and coalesces small allocations at epoch boundaries triggered by cache eviction.
4) Continuous batching interplay: modify the batching planner to account for model_profile headroom, treating pre-reserved KV slabs as non-evictable when estimating available capacity for new batched requests; when headroom < threshold, trigger immediate partial flush/fallthrough to smaller model variant (e.g., 70B -> 70B-8bit) based on routing policy.
5) Tests and metrics: microbenchmarks (single pod), integration tests (dedicated capacity), and stability testing under synthetic spike patterns. Capture latency P50/P95, throughput, OOM count, and token cost.

Acceptance criteria:
- Model_profile loader exists and is exercised by the model onboarding flow.
- Regression tests show <=2% latency increase at P95 vs baseline when applying profiles under typical loads.
- Fragmentation overhead reduced >=18% measured by maximum resident allocations vs compacted baseline on target pod shapes.
- Continuous batching planner uses profile headroom and avoids at least 90% of previously observed frag-induced OOMs in the test harness.

Open trade-offs:
- Pre-reserving KV slabs improves fragmentation but may increase committed GPU memory and impact multi-tenant utilization. We will experiment with dynamic slab sizes and conservative defaults.
- Coalescing at epoch boundaries adds complexity to KV eviction semantics; must ensure correctness for cached attention state during partial rollouts.

Implementation milestones:
- 2025-02-14: profiling harness and heatmap outputs for three model variants (done)
- 2025-02-20: initial profile spec and allocator hook PR (in review)
- 2025-02-25: continuous-batching planner adjustments and integration tests
- 2025-02-28: rollout to dedicated canary pool and observability dashboards
- 2025-03-01: full rollout to runtime-1.22 if metrics pass

Related artifacts: Design doc: drive.redwood/reports/model_contiguity_design_v1 (link pending). Benchmarks: gh:redwood-inference/runtime-benchmarks/pulls/421.

Notes for reviewers: focus on allocator safety (no silent fallbacks that can corrupt KV), clear semantics for pre-reserved slabs, and compatibility with quantized execution paths.

2025-02-12 — Diego Alvarez: Implemented heatmap parser and a first-pass contiguity map generator. Early results show fragmentation hot spots near layer 22-28 (middle layers) for Llama-2-70b. Open PR: gh:redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1987

2025-02-14 — SRE (Priya Rao): Ran long-duration soak with continuous batching enabled. Saw 7 OOMs in 24h on dedicated-2xA100 testbed without profile applied. With profile applied proto-allocator, OOMs dropped to 1 (still investigating edge-case).

2025-02-15 — Diego Alvarez: Changed default KV allocation alignment from 256B to 1KB for quantized kernels which reduced small-fragment leftover by ~9%. Added unit tests for slab allocation and buddy fallback.

2025-02-16 — Product (Liam Chen): Confirmed tolerance for small P95 latency bump in exchange for throughput gains. Requested that rollout gate include token-cost dashboard update and customer-impact tag for any test failures.

2025-02-18 — Diego Alvarez: Allocator hook PR updated with safety checks and feature flag runtime.memory_model_profiles. Ready for staging canary. Next: adjust batching planner to consult profile headroom API (work scheduled 2025-02-19).
